title: Median Days Between Customer Purchases
description:
For each customer, calculate the **median number of days between consecutive purchases** using `PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5)`. Only consider gaps between actual orders (ignore first-order rows with no prior purchase).

**Table: orders** — `order_id`, `customer_id`, `order_date`

Output columns: `customer_id`, `median_days_between`. Order by `customer_id`.
solution_sql: WITH intervals AS (SELECT customer_id, order_date, (order_date - LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date)) AS days_between FROM orders) SELECT customer_id, PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_between) AS median_days_between FROM intervals WHERE days_between IS NOT NULL GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY customer_id;

test_cases.description: Customer 1 gaps {14,36,24} median=24; Customer 2 gaps {31,29,41} median=31; Customer 3 gaps {31,29} median=30

hints: Use LAG(order_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date) then subtract to get days_between. DuckDB DATE - DATE = INTEGER.
Filter WHERE days_between IS NOT NULL to exclude the first order per customer (which has no prior order).
PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_between) computes the median, interpolating between values when needed.
explanation: Customer 1 gaps: Jan 1→Jan 15 = 14 days, Jan 15→Feb 20 = 36 days, Feb 20→Mar 15 = 24 days. Sorted: {14,24,36} → median = 24. Customer 2: Jan 10→Feb 10=31, Feb 10→Mar 10=29, Mar 10→Apr 20=41. Sorted: {29,31,41} → median = 31. Customer 3: Jan 5→Feb 5=31, Feb 5→Mar 5=29. Sorted: {29,31} → PERCENTILE_CONT interpolates = 30.0.
